title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.67
exact_target: Can the Fitting height of a finite soluble group be bounded using only an automorphism order and the Prüfer rank of its fixed-point subgroup?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
For a finite group $K$, let $d(K)$ be the least number of generators
needed to generate $K$, with $d(1)=0$. Its Pr\"ufer rank is
\[
 \operatorname{rk}(K)=\max\{d(L):L\le K\}.
\]
Thus every subgroup, not only $K$ itself, must be generated by at most
this many elements. A bound on rank need not bound the order of $K$.

Let $G$ be a finite soluble group and $\phi\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$.
Set $m=|\phi|$ and
$r=\operatorname{rk}(C_G(\phi))$, where
$C_G(\phi)=\{g\in G:\phi(g)=g\}$.
Soluble means that repeated commutator subgroups eventually become
trivial. Its Fitting height $h(G)$ is the least length of a normal
series with nilpotent factors. Nilpotent means that iterating
$\gamma_{i+1}(L)=[\gamma_i(L),L]$, starting with $\gamma_1(L)=L$,
eventually gives $1$.

Does there exist a function $f(m,r)$ such that
$h(G)\le f(m,r)$ for all such $G$ and $\phi$?
The bound must be independent of the order, exponent, and particular
structure of the fixed-point subgroup, apart from its rank. It must
also be independent of $|G|$.

No coprimality of $m$ and $|G|$ is assumed, and $m$ may have arbitrarily
many prime divisors. The assertion concerns the whole group $G$; it
does not permit passing to a subgroup or quotient to obtain the
height bound. Rank zero is allowed when $C_G(\phi)=1$.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Can the Fitting height of a finite soluble group be bounded using only an automorphism order and the Prüfer rank of its fixed-point subgroup?
